fixes.explanation: Yes, baker. The writer says, “Instead, those sacrifices are an annual reminder of sins…” Every year they brought the sins back to mind instead of ending them. It's like a bill that shows up in the mailbox every year, a reminder that it's still there.

You've got it, baker. When Christ came into the world, He said, “Sacrifice and offering You did not desire…” (Hebrews 10:5) He is speaking to God here. Then He adds that God took no delight in burnt offerings and sin offerings (Hebrews 10:6).

This one is actually true, friend. The writer replays Christ's words about sacrifices and offerings God did not desire. Then he adds a note: “(although they are offered according to the law).” So the card matches the text.

Once, baker. The writer says we have been sanctified through the sacrifice of the body of Jesus Christ “…once for all…” One time, not year after year and not day after day. That's the difference from the sacrifices the priests kept offering (Hebrews 10:1, 11).

That's right, baker. The writer says that when this Priest had offered for all time one sacrifice for sins, “…He sat down at the right hand of God.” Compare that to the priests, who stand day after day to offer the same sacrifices again and again (Hebrews 10:11). One Priest sits, and the others keep standing.

Not quite, friend. The writer says that day after day every priest stands to minister and to offer the same sacrifices again and again (Hebrews 10:11). But this Priest offered one sacrifice for sins for all time, and then “…He sat down at the right hand of God.” So He sat down.

The wilderness isn't in this verse, baker. The writer says that after offering one sacrifice for sins for all time, Jesus “…sat down at the right hand of God.” That is a very different picture from the priest who stands day after day (Hebrews 10:11).

True, baker. The writer says, “Since that time, He waits for His enemies to be made a footstool for His feet…” So after sitting down at the right hand of God, Jesus waits. That's why my ovens stay ready, though the text never says when.

Perfect, baker. The writer says, “…by a single offering He has made perfect for all time those who are being sanctified.” One offering, and the result is for all time. That's the same one sacrifice the writer pointed to in verse 12.

Strong is a fine word, baker, but the writer uses a different one. He says Jesus “…has made perfect for all time…” and he says it of “…those who are being sanctified.” The word is perfect, and it comes by a single offering, not repeated ones.

Careful, friend, that's the opposite of what the Lord says. He says, “Their sins and lawless acts I will remember no more.” Under the old sacrifices, the writer says, there was “…an annual reminder of sins…” (Hebrews 10:3). But here the Lord says He will remember their sins no more.
